analysis: The Culture option is the closest provisional response. It combines museum and heritage study, cultural and art history, public memory, film and literature with rhetorical, sociological and research work. The museum and heritage courses address defining exact-target substance. The schedule does not replicate the required placement or teacher training.

The digital option approaches media and identity through critical analysis, data, image processing, predictive modelling and ethics. The formal English family route supports this emphasis. Databases provide data handling and are complementary. Introductory Brain & Behavior provides the formal lead-in to Psycholinguistics, which adds a bounded perspective on language and communication. Move Psycholinguistics to term two and qualitative methods to term six. Substitute AI Ethics for evidence synthesis to strengthen privacy, fairness and accountability without suggesting AI engineering or online politics as standalone qualifications.

The education-related option combines language and literary interpretation, social influence, development, youth prevention and quantitative research. The absence of compulsory pedagogy or teacher certification remains explicit. Shift introductory Sociology to term one, Modern Sociology to term three and Brain & Behavior to term four before Lifespan Developmental Psychology. All three programmes are feasible and distinct.

Replaced generic paired claims with evidenced thematic or methodological overlaps in heritage, museums, modern Europe, public spheres, media, nature and society, ethnographic methods and rhetoric. The unresolved external final-year components do not support positive alignments. The optional independent research provision is separate from scheduled credits.

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning

DISDATA212.contribution: Uses computational techniques to process and interpret digital images. Its focus is technical image analysis.

GOSHIST111.name: Modern History
GOSHIST111.contribution: Investigates political, economic and cultural modernity from 1815 through industrialisation, nationhood and ideological change.

GOSHIST312.name: Researching the “American Century”
GOSHIST312.contribution: Builds a historical research project on the American century through question design and critical source analysis.

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.contribution: Uses competing theories and philosophical argument to evaluate ethical questions.

GOSPOLI111.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
GOSPOLI111.contribution: Uses historical and contemporary political thought to reason about rights, society and political authority.

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: Introduces sociological explanations of solidarity, inequality, identity and exclusion.

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: Develops ethically grounded qualitative research design, data collection, analysis and communication.

GOSSOCI214.name: Modern Sociology
GOSSOCI214.contribution: Examines modern sociological theory through critical perspectives on modernity, exclusion and colonialism.

GOSSOCI215.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
GOSSOCI215.contribution: Uses case studies to explore social movements, environmental justice and collective action.

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
GOSSOCI311.contribution: Uses contemporary social theory to analyse civil society, public spheres, hegemony, solidarity and social movements.

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.contribution: Studies comprehension, production, acquisition and bilingualism through psychological and neurobiological approaches.

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.contribution: Introduces cognitive and neuroscientific accounts of learning and behaviour and prepares students for later psychology courses.

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: Examines social cognition, influence, persuasion and group behaviour.

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: Designs behavioural experiments and interprets and checks multivariable statistical models.

HCBPSYC314.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
HCBPSYC314.contribution: Studies cognitive, social and emotional development from prenatal life to old age.

HCBPSYC315.name: Youth Resilience to Extremism
HCBPSYC315.contribution: Analyses youth radicalisation, adolescent risk and protective factors, and educational prevention.

MCCCOMM111.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
MCCCOMM111.contribution: Analyses argument, rhetorical form and delivery, with practice in persuasive communication.

MCCCOMM211.name: Style & Meaning
MCCCOMM211.contribution: Analyses how grammar, deixis and other linguistic choices shape effects in literary and nonfiction texts.

MCCCOMM212.name: Communicating the Climate Crisis
MCCCOMM212.contribution: Examines public communication of climate issues through texts, film, exhibitions, protest art and social media.

MCCCOMM213.name: Rhetoric in Action
MCCCOMM213.contribution: Develops and adapts public-speaking, storytelling and debating activities with primary-school children.

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: Evaluates framing, argument and ethical persuasion, applying these to community-engaged work.

MCCCOMM312.name: Creative Communication Laboratory
MCCCOMM312.contribution: Uses poetry, performance and experimental practice to explore and communicate artistic ideas.

MCCHEAM111.name: Introduction to Western Art History
MCCHEAM111.contribution: Relates Western visual art from the late medieval period to contemporary practice to religious, political and cultural change.

MCCHEAM211.name: African Art & Heritage
MCCHEAM211.contribution: Examines African visual traditions, their cultural meanings and the interpretation and display of heritage.

MCCHEAM212.name: Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean
MCCHEAM212.contribution: Studies Renaissance Italian art and architecture through artistic exchanges across the Mediterranean.

MCCHEAM312.name: Modern Art & Modern Museums
MCCHEAM312.contribution: Connects modern and contemporary artworks to museums, exhibitions and the institutions that shape public reception.

MCCHEAM316.name: Writing Art's Histories
MCCHEAM316.contribution: Critiques how art historians have interpreted visual culture and constructed the discipline over time.

MCCLITR111.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
MCCLITR111.contribution: Uses close reading and genre to interpret fiction, poetry, drama and nonfiction, with an introduction to film adaptation.

MCCLITR112.name: Great Literary Works
MCCLITR112.contribution: Compares major literary works across periods through questions of freedom, gender, community and mortality.

MCCLITR211.name: World Myth & Literature
MCCLITR211.contribution: Compares mythic narratives across traditions and studies their transmission and treatment of power, love and gender.

MCCLITR212.name: Life & Travel Writing
MCCLITR212.contribution: Examines how memoir, travel writing and digital self-presentation construct memory and identity.

MCCLITR311.name: Film & Text
MCCLITR311.contribution: Compares how literary narratives and their film adaptations use their different forms to tell stories.

MCCLITR312.name: Perspectives on Literary Meaning
MCCLITR312.contribution: Applies theories of reading and interpretation to a literary research project.

MCCMEDI111.name: Introduction to Film & Media
MCCMEDI111.contribution: Uses editing, sound, cinematography, narrative and performance to explain how moving images create meaning.

MCCMEDI112.name: Media Archaeology
MCCMEDI112.contribution: Interprets communication technologies from print and early recording to networks as historical and cultural objects.

MCCMEDI211.name: From T.V. to TikTok
MCCMEDI211.contribution: Studies power, social history and representation in US television, film and contemporary digital media.

MCCMEDI212.name: Media & the Environment
MCCMEDI212.contribution: Analyses how media shape ecological understanding and how people represent human and nonhuman relationships.

MCCMEDI311.name: Media & Race
MCCMEDI311.contribution: Investigates race, representation and power through American media and popular culture.

MCCMEDI312.name: The Documentary
MCCMEDI312.contribution: Studies the ethics, aesthetics and history of nonfiction representation and develops practical documentary work.

alignment.rationale: Both study the cultural meaning of heritage. UCR focuses on African visual traditions and questions about their interpretation and display.
Both study the role of museums. UCR focuses on how museums and exhibitions shape the display and reception of modern art.
Both study transformations in modern Europe. UCR starts in 1815 and uses a wider historical and geographical frame.
Both examine how media technologies shape culture. UCR approaches digital networks through the history of earlier media.
Both examine popular media and social life. UCR uses examples from American television, film and digital media.
Both examine media and power. UCR focuses on race and representation in American cultural history.
Both explore changing ideas about human relationships with nature. UCR studies how media shape those ideas.
Both address public spheres. UCR situates them within contemporary theories of civil society and social movements.
Both develop qualitative inquiry. UCR covers qualitative research design, collection and analysis across a wider range of social research.
Both study persuasive communication. UCR draws on classical rhetoric and applies it through analysis and practice.
